- 为什么做：属于「知识检索平台化」专题第二阶段；实现改动 #37256（让索引文档记下所属组织、检索时先按组织过滤）改了指纹的算法，按这份记录自己的规矩，这种改动要先以带日期的说明写进记录、由你批准。
- 出错会怎样：说明写错的话，后面写存储适配器的人会照着错的做，最坏是换了组织的文档在重建索引时被跳过、在按组织过滤的检索里排不上；这次只有文档，撤回这次合并即可。
- 要你做什么：审后由你本人合并（合并即批准），并且要排在实现改动 #37256（上面那个让文档记下所属组织的改动）之前合并。

## What changes

One file under `docs/adr/`: `0161-knowledge-platform-boundary-platform-owns-assembly-sync-split-record-return-knowledge-source-is-a-governed-type.md`, 9 lines added and none removed against `main`. No schema, no code, no changeset.

**This PR must merge before PR #37256.** That PR changes the hash recipe of K8 item 2, and K8 rule 3 gives the form of such a change: "the change is a dated note on this record". Contract review `7157191417` on PR #37256 (its finding M1) and the seat's L1 `7157210840` hold that PR until this note has merged. `docs/adr/**` is Tier H: the maintainer merges this PR; no seat approves, merges or enqueues it.

`Part of #37097`, not a closing line: the card's implementation is PR #37256 and stays there. This PR carries the record's note and nothing else.

Two additions, both in the form sibling records already use (ADR-0090 and ADR-0151, notes of 2026-11-24):

1. **A dated note under K8's table**, as a blockquote that opens `Note (2026-11-25, card, built by PR)`. The table is left as written.
2. **One `Amended` bullet at the end of the header list**, pointing at the note. The `Status:` line is byte-identical, so the generated `docs/adr/README.md` does not change and is not in the diff.

The note, as it stands at the head:

> **Note (2026-11-25, [#37097](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/37097), built by [#37256](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/37256)) — items 2 and 9: the hash covers the organization of a document that has one.** Item 2's hash covers the document as the service assembles it. The parenthesis "content, title, metadata" was everything assembly set on a document, its identity aside, when item 2 was accepted. Item 9 adds `organizationId` to the assembled document when the document has one, and the hash covers it then. A document without one hashes byte for byte as it did before, so the version prefix is not bumped.
>
> - **Why.** A document that gains an organization, loses it or moves to another one gets a new hash, so a complete reindex never leaves a stale organization on a stored document. The other answer kept the parenthesis and bumped the version. It leaves a later change of organization to the events alone, and missed events are the hole reconcile exists to close (K1).
> - **A later optional member that assembly sets** enters the hash the same way, left out when it is absent, or the version is bumped.
> - **What an adapter stores.** An adapter that stores `docHash` stores `organizationId` from the same version on; otherwise, once it starts reading this field, a complete reindex skips its documents and a walled search never ranks them.
>
> Item 9's first reader, #37097, is built by PR #37256, and this change to item 2 lands with it. The reasoning is contract review [`7157191417`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/37256#issuecomment-7157191417) on that PR (its M1 and S2). The table is left as written; read items 2 and 9 with this note.

The header bullet:

> - **Amended** (2026-11-25, [#37097](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/37097)): a dated note under the table of [K8](#k8--the-contract-additions-decided-item-by-item) records that the document hash of item 2 covers `organizationId` when the document has one (item 9), with no version bump. The status line above is left as it is.

| the hash covered content, title and metadata | `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service.ts#computeDocHash` on `origin/main` at `d62f9e9c` |
| assembly also sets the document's identity, which the hash never covered | `recordToDocument` in the same file at `d62f9e9c`: `id`, `sourceId`, `sourceRecordId` beside `content`, `title`, `metadata` |
| the organization enters the hashed body only when the document has one; the version stays `v1` | `computeDocHash` and `DOC_HASH_VERSION` on PR #37256's branch at `e8b0688f` (and unchanged from `3df745d2`, the head the review read) |
| events keep an index fresh, reconcile keeps it correct | K1 of this record, the "Sync and reconcile" row |
| the adapter sentence | finding S2 of review `7157191417`; character for character the spec TSDoc on `KnowledgeDocument.organizationId` on PR #37256 at `6e978db3` |

## Acceptance notes

- **Where the note's words differ from the dispatch order's summary**, each for precision:
  - The order's summary says the item 9 reader "landed" in PR #37256. This note merges first, so it says the reader "is built by PR #37256, and this change to item 2 lands with it", which is true before and after that merge.
  - "The whole assembled document" became "everything assembly set on a document, its identity aside": assembly also sets `id`, `sourceId` and `sourceRecordId`, and the hash never covered those.
  - The rule for a later optional member is scoped to a member "that assembly sets", so it does not read as a rule about every optional key of `KnowledgeDocument` (the chunk channel of item 5 is set by the splitter and belongs to K7's fingerprint).
  - The adapter sentence is the spec TSDoc's sentence on PR #37256, word for word (commit `aec56080`), so the record and the contract say the same thing.
- **The header bullet** was not in the order's list. It follows ADR-0151, whose header has the same shape and gains one `Amended` bullet per dated note.
- **The note cites the review record** `7157191417`, so that the approver finds the reasoning from the record itself.
- **No `scripts/adr-anchors` entry.** `pnpm check:adr-anchors` exits 0 without one, so the gate does not require it for the note. The review's N4 (an anchor for K8 item 9 in code) stays a follow-up outside this file surface.
- **No changeset.** `docs/adr/**` publishes nothing and no derived gate asked for one; the PR carries `skip-changeset`.
- **PR #37256 moved while this was written**, from `3df745d2` (the head the review read) to `6e978db3`. What changed there is a test file and the spec TSDoc; the hash recipe is the same at every head.

## Verification

Read first:

1. The note under K8's table in the one changed file. The sentence to weigh is the adapter rule, "An adapter that stores `docHash` stores `organizationId` from the same version on": K8 rule 2 keeps every member optional, and this sentence says two of them are taken up together.
2. The "Why" bullet of the same note: it records which answer was not taken (keep the parenthesis, bump the version) and why.
3. `computeDocHash` on PR #37256's branch, `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service.ts`, to hold the note against the recipe it describes.
